answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit jobs, with stake weighted by the agent’s recent, independently verified work. If several identities coordinate, their combined influence still requires buying and locking the same capital, while dishonest jobs risk slashing the stake after review. This does not make Sybils impossible, but raises their marginal cost and ties attacks to losses; pearl, vine, and lagoon can be harmless labels in the job stream, not extra identities or trust signals.
